title: 1.2.5 Change the Type
description: Give one variable three different types in a row and print what typeof says each time. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Declare it as a string
steps.instructions: Declare a variable called `thing` with `let` and set it to any piece of text in quotes.

steps.title: Print its type
hints: typeof goes immediately before the value you are asking about
The answer comes back as a word in quotes - that is normal
You will use this line three times, once after each change

steps.title: Reassign it to a number
steps.instructions: Set `thing` to a number. Do NOT declare it again with let, just assign to it.

steps.title: Reassign it to a boolean, printing the type after each change
steps.instructions: Set `thing` to true or false, and print typeof thing after each reassignment so you can see the type change.

requirements.title: thing is declared with let
requirements.description: Declares a variable called thing using let. Help: 1.2.4 (Dynamically Typed)

requirements.title: thing starts as a string
requirements.description: thing holds text in quotes, whether from its own let or a later assignment. Help: 1.2.4 (Dynamically Typed)

requirements.title: thing is reassigned without let
requirements.description: Assigns a new value to thing without re-declaring it. Help: 1.2.4 (Dynamically Typed)

requirements.title: thing is given a boolean
requirements.description: At some point thing holds true or false, either literally or from a comparison. Help: 1.2.4 (Dynamically Typed)

requirements.title: typeof is printed
requirements.description: Uses console.log with typeof thing to show the type. Help: 1.2.4 (Dynamically Typed)
